sources: npm registry audit API via pnpm audit
Docker Hub image index via docker buildx imagetools inspect
GitHub releases API for pinned Actions

python.requirements-base.lock.txt: no known vulnerabilities (production images install only this lock)
python.requirements.lock.txt / requirements-fal: chromadb 1.5.9 (no fix published), filelock 3.32.7 (fixed in 4.2.1, blocked; see limitations)

securityChanges: Override @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent>undici to 8.12.3: pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 still pins undici 8.10.2 exactly, which carries 9 advisories (TLS certificate validation bypass, cross-user cache poisoning, several DoS); server already declares 8.12.3 directly
Override express>body-parser to ^2.4.0 (DoS via trailing bytes, reached through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk express transport)

Override ajv>fast-uri to ^3.1.9 (URI scheme spoofing, host confusion); @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.4.0 inlines its own fast-uri 3.1.8 in dist/ajvProvider-*.mjs, which no override reaches and pnpm audit cannot see. It only resolves $id/$ref in our server-defined schemas, not tool input; track the next SDK release
Node 24.21.0 -> 24.22.1 (2026-10-20 security release) in server and worker images by refreshing node:24-*-slim digests

@node-saml/node-saml 5.1.0 -> 5.2.0: checks idpIssuer on the Response and assertion, rejects multiple Issuers, fixes maxAssertionAgeMs skipping; DocSlurp already passes idpIssuer from IdP metadata and uses only the POST binding
docker/login-action v4.6.0 -> v4.7.0 and github/codeql-action/upload-sarif v4.39.0 -> v4.39.1, pinned by commit SHA

compatibilityHolds.openai: 6.49.0: 7.x is a major API change; held with the AI SDK family
compatibilityHolds.opentelemetry: 2.12/0.223/API 1.9.1: 3.0/0.300 is a breaking family change; Langfuse 6 requires SDK 2
compatibilityHolds.filelock: 3.32.7 in dev-only ML locks: forcing >=4.2.1 downgrades unstructured 0.27.33 -> 0.20.8 (unstructured caps filelock<4)
compatibilityHolds.@mastra/core: 1.79.0: 1.80.0 was ~3h old at audit time and @mastra/* is exempt from minimumReleaseAge; revisit next round

limitations: ChromaDB 1.5.9 advisories have no published fix; DocSlurp uses HttpClient/PersistentClient for the optional vector backend, not the Chroma HTTP server, and production images do not install it
Worker images were not rebuilt or smoke-tested here; the digest refresh takes effect on the next worker-images run
No production deployment, model download or hosted quality evaluation was run

validation.checkout: standalone core worktree at the audited commit (CI layout)

workerTests.failures: local-artifact-adapters.test.ts 5-second timeouts under full-suite load (same file as the 2026-10-21 audit); passes 4/4 in isolation

validation.notes: Server tests read the developer .env through findWorkspaceRoot and fail spuriously when one with chat MCP keys is present; results above were run without one

resolved: bundled fast-uri 3.1.8 in MCP server: documented above
followUps: Pre-existing: SAML request cache accepts unconsumed-or-consumed unexpired rows and has a no-op removeAsync, so a captured signed response can be replayed within the request window; implement consumeAsync/saveIfAbsentAsync, set rejectReplayedAssertions, bind InResponseTo to RelayState (sso.ts:517-560)
Pre-existing: idpIssuer is undefined when IdP metadata lacks entityID, disabling the issuer check; treat missing entityID as an error (sso.ts:364, :968)
Add a signed SAMLResponse round-trip test with wrong-issuer, multiple-Issuer and unsigned negatives
Rebuild worker images and run the Doppler guest and corrupt/oversized-PDF smoke tests before deploying
